messages:
Devon: quick idea — propose we support ephemeral cross-org delegation tokens for 3rd-party integrations. short-lived token that allows caller from Org A to act on Project B with scoped rights, but preserves clear billing/quota attribution and audit trail. thoughts?
Marta: hmm important for partners. main questions: who gets billed? quota counting? telemetry surfaces? :thinking_face:
Jasper: technically we can add an "orig_org" claim in the token JWT and ensure router attributes requests with (orig_org, target_project). billing can attribute to orig_org or target_project depending on product decision.
Dina: revocation + propagation is hairy, esp for Private deployments with relaxed control-plane connectivity. we need TTL + active revocation lists pushed to edge or KV with versioning. also KMS keys for signing.
policy-bot: Policy ticket created: RDW-3421 - delegation-token-spec (assignee: TBD) :white_check_mark:
Akira: console UX note — dropdown to select "on behalf of" org/project when creating token, with an option to require approval chain. show TTL slider and a checkbox "audit all actions". keep default TTL short (1h).
Devon: sample header I was thinking about: 
```
Authorization: Bearer <delegation-jwt>
X-Redwood-Delegation: orig_org=org_A;target_project=proj_B;ttl=3600
```
Jasper: router implications: routing cache keys must include orig_org to avoid misattributing sessions. and we need deterministic fallback if target_project denies billing from orig_org.
Marta: telemetry needs: per-token tags (orig_org, requester_id, project, route), and a flag to show "delegated" in cost dashboards. also alerts when delegated traffic > X% of spend.
Dina: security: require a signed consent record for cross-org delegation, stored immutably for audits. also ensure impersonation flag is explicit so logs show "acted-as: org_A/serviceX".
Akira: rollout idea: feature-flag for runtime + console. start internal-only, then customer opt-in, canary 5% + 25% + full. include a migration toggle for legacy tokens.
Devon: ops concern — private deploys: Dina, any thoughts on a push model vs pull revocation for air-gapped setups?
Dina: push is better but not always possible. fallback: short TTL + telemetry that surfaces long-lived delegated tokens. also provide an offline revocation file distribution mechanism.
Jasper: one more: update quota engine to support "charge_to" override with safety checks (prevent cross-org cost leakage). we should gate that behind org-level billing permission.
Marta: I'll draft telemetry schema and dashboard mockups. labels: delegated:true, orig_org, target_project, requester.
Devon: ok owners: Marta (telemetry/dashboard), Jasper (runtime/router/quotas), Dina (security/revocation/KMS), Akira (console/UX). I'll create the design doc and link the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
policy-bot: RFC created: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/rdw-3421 (status: draft)
Akira: for follow-up meeting, morning sync tomorrow? 10:30am PT works?
Marta: works for me.
Jasper: yep.
Dina: 👍
Devon: added to calendar.
